binders: A sample-space type Ω equipped with a measurable space.
A measure μ on Ω equipped with the assumption that μ is finite.
A finite family X indexed by ι, where each X i is a real-valued function on Ω.
hypotheses: For every index i, X i belongs to MemLp at exponent 2 with respect to μ.
For every pair of distinct indices i and j, the functions X i and X j are independent with respect to μ.
conclusions: The variance with respect to μ of the pointwise sum over all i of X i equals the sum over all i of the variances with respect to μ of X i.
mathematical_definitions: The sum over i is finite because ι is a Fintype and is taken over Finset.univ.
The function sum is pointwise: at each ω in Ω, its value is the finite sum of X i ω over all i.
MemLp at exponent 2 means almost-everywhere strong measurability together with finite extended L2 norm.
The independence condition is pairwise independence for distinct indices, not an explicit assertion of mutual independence of the whole family.
Variance is the real number obtained by converting the extended variance to Real.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For any finite family of real-valued square-integrable functions on a finite measure space, if every two functions with different indices are independent with respect to the measure, then the variance of their pointwise finite sum is equal to the sum of their individual variances.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The measure is assumed finite but is not explicitly assumed to be a probability measure or to have total mass one.
Only pairwise independence of functions with distinct indices is required.
The index type may be empty; then the square-integrability and independence hypotheses are vacuous and both sides concern empty sums.
A singleton index type makes the independence hypothesis vacuous.
The hypotheses use MemLp, so measurability is only required in its almost-everywhere strong form.
Variance is defined through conversion from an extended variance to a real number; the L2 hypotheses are the stated finiteness control.
All L2, independence, and variance assertions use the same measure μ.
ambiguities: In informal probability language, variance and independence are commonly stated for probability measures, whereas the formal proposition assumes only that μ is finite.
The packet gives the kernel-based formal definition of IndepFun but does not expand its event-level mathematical characterization.
